newsitem.title: USA: Amre Inc stock buyers file class action.
newsitem.headline: Amre Inc stock buyers file class action.

text.p: A lawfirm representing purchasers of Amre Inc common stock said on Wednesday that it had filed a class action suit charging that Amre officials misrepresented the relationship between their company and HFS Inc, thus artificially inflating the price of Amre common stock.
HFS is also charged with misreprenting information about the strength and nature of its relationship to Amre, the firm said.
The stock buyers, who bought Amre stock between Sept. 3 and Jan. 17, are represented by Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP.
The complaint charges that the defendants knew that the relationship between the two companies was significantly weaker than they publicly represented, Milberg Weiss said.
Ultimately, as a result of HFS's withdrawal of financial support for Amre, Amre was forced into bankruptcy, it added.

"While certain material information was concealed from investors, Amre insiders unloaded large blocks of Amre stock at artificially inflated prices, reaping huge profits in excess of $2.5 million," the lawfirm said.
It added that the share buyers sought to recover damages in the case, but it declined to discuss an amount.

"As we understand the complaint, we believe it is without merit and we intend to defend it vigorously," said HFS executive vice president at general counsel, James Buckman. He added that HFS had not yet been served with the complaint.
HFS franchises hotels and residential real estate brokerage offices.
